issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Lemma 2.1 applies the Woodbury matrix inversion formula without inverting the inner bracketed term $(I_n + M^T (	ilde{\lambda} I_r)^{-1} M)^{-1}$. This produces the erroneous matrix equations (2.3) and (2.4), which claim that $(	ilde{\lambda} I_r + M M^T)^{-1} = \frac{1}{\tilde{\lambda}} I_r - \frac{1}{\tilde{\lambda}^3} M (M^T M + \tilde{\lambda} I_n) M^T$. For scalar $M=1$ and $\tilde{\lambda}=1$, the left-hand side is $1/2$ while the right-hand side is $-1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the proof with the standard one-line identity $(M^T M + \tilde{\lambda} I_n) M^T = M^T (M M^T + \tilde{\lambda} I_r)$, and multiply on the left by $(M^T M + \tilde{\lambda} I_n)^{-1}$ and on the right by $(M M^T + \tilde{\lambda} I_r)^{-1}$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma 2.1 is invalid as written, though the statement itself is true.
issues.title: Invalid proof of matrix identity using erroneous Woodbury formula
issues.why_classification: The stated lemma statement is mathematically correct, and a routine one-line algebraic argument replaces the proof without affecting any dependent results.

issues.failure_explanation: In Theorem 2.3, the error relation is $x_{t+1} - x_\star = \tilde{\lambda}(A_\tau^T A_\tau + \tilde{\lambda} I)^{-1}(x_t - x_\star)$. The proof bounds the operator norm by replacing the minimum eigenvalue with the smallest non-zero eigenvalue $\lambda_{\min}^+(A_\tau^T A_\tau)$. However, since $A_\tau$ has size $k \times n$ with $k < n$, $A_\tau^T A_\tau$ is rank-deficient and has eigenvalue 0 with multiplicity at least $n - k$. On the null space $\mathcal{N}(A_\tau)$, the operator $\tilde{\lambda}(A_\tau^T A_\tau + \tilde{\lambda} I)^{-1}$ acts as the identity with eigenvalue $\frac{\tilde{\lambda}}{0 + \tilde{\lambda}} = 1$. Because $x_t - x_\star$ lies in $\mathcal{R}(A^T)$ rather than $\mathcal{R}(A_\tau^T)$, it has a nonzero component in $\mathcal{N}(A_\tau)$ that is unattenuated by the update. The claimed contraction bound is false and would absurdly imply that taking $\tilde{\lambda} \to 0$ solves any system in a single block update.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish a valid convergence proof for regularized block Kaczmarz that analyzes the expectation over the choice of blocks across the full matrix $A$, yielding a contraction rate governed by the spectrum of the global matrix $A$ rather than $\frac{\tilde{\lambda}}{\lambda_{\min}^{\text{block}} + \tilde{\lambda}}$.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 2.3 is false: neither the deterministic step bound nor the expected exponential convergence rate holds as stated.
issues.title: False error contraction bound ignoring zero eigenvalues of block Gram matrix
issues.why_classification: The central theoretical convergence guarantee of the paper for Algorithm 1 fails completely, and no local correction can preserve the claimed contraction rate.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 4.2 claims that iterates of Algorithm 1 converge in expectation to $x^{(\mu)}$ by invoking Theorem 4.1 of [15] (ReRBK). However, Theorem 4.1 of ReRBK strictly requires blocks to be sampled from a fixed probability distribution $\mu$ independently of the current iterate $x_j$. Algorithm 1 includes an adaptive, deterministic step (Step 10) that selects row indices $\mathcal{I}$ corresponding to the largest squared entries of the residual $b - A x_j$. Because $\mathcal{I}$ depends nonlinearly on $x_j$, the blocks are not drawn from a fixed distribution independent of $x_j$, and the conditional expectation relation $\mathbb{E}[x_{j+1} \mid x_j] = (I - \bar{P}) x_j + \dots$ fails. Thus, the hypotheses of the invoked result do not hold.

failure_location.quote: The proof follows from the Theorem 4.1 in \cite{ReRBK}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must formulate a convergence proof that accounts for the nonlinear residual-dependent greedy selection step or restrict the claim to an algorithm that omits the adaptive greedy step.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee that Algorithm 1 converges in expectation to the weighted least-squares solution $x^{(\mu)}$ is unestablished.
issues.title: Misapplication of ReRBK convergence theorem to an adaptive hybrid algorithm
issues.why_classification: The claim relies on an external theorem whose fundamental independence premise is violated by the proposed algorithm, requiring an entirely new proof architecture for hybrid randomized/greedy iterations.
